title: Breakfast Crunchwraps
subtitle: Griddled tortilla bundles with eggs, hash, and a crunchy tostada center.
description: Inspired by the drive-through classic but built for ten hungry firefighters. Each crunchwrap stacks eggs, sausage, cheese, and a crisp tostada inside a large flour tortilla, folded hex-style and griddled until golden and structurally sound.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Breakfast Crunchwraps in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Sausage. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep all fillings
steps.instruction: Crisp hash browns on a lightly oiled griddle in a thin layer, season with salt, and hold warm. Brown sausage and drain. Soft-scramble eggs last so they stay tender. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Plan about 15 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts.

steps.title: Set the build station
steps.instruction: Lay out tortillas, tostadas, cheese sauce, and a small bowl of cheese slices cut to seal the bottom fold. Warm nacho cheese so it spreads without tearing tortillas. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Stack and fold
steps.instruction: Center tostada on tortilla, layer hash, sausage, eggs, cheddar, and a drizzle of nacho cheese. Fold edges to center in a hex pattern; place a cheese slice on the bottom seam to glue it shut. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Griddle both sides
steps.instruction: Cook seam-side down on a medium griddle with a light press until golden and sealed, 3–4 minutes. Flip carefully and griddle the top until crisp and cheese melts through. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Serve immediately
steps.instruction: Cut in half on a bias for the line or serve whole in parchment wraps. Hold finished wraps in a 200°F oven seam-side down—don't stack or you'll lose the crunch. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: One cook runs the griddle press while another builds—pre-cut all seal cheese slices before the rush.
Keep tostadas in a warm dry pan so they stay shatter-crisp until the moment of assembly.
Build in batches of four; griddle while the next batch stacks so nothing sits and steams.
cleanupNotes: Scrape the griddle between batches with a bench scraper while still warm to prevent cheese carbon buildup.
Wipe the press or second skillet with a damp towel held by tongs—never submerge hot cast iron.
leftovers: Crunchwraps do not hold well; plan portions tightly and turn extras into deconstructed bowls with salsa.
If you must reheat, use a dry skillet over low heat with a lid—microwave destroys the tostada crunch.
